lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The current Agent recognizes a closed client-side command grammar and maps it only to navigation, source intake, contact drafting, page review, and next-move navigation. The product boundary is correct, but the operation proposal and receipt are not yet enforced by a server-side capability registry.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/agent-ui-command.ts returns one of five typed commands or null; apps/web/components/relationship-workspace-app.tsx keeps external effects outside runAgentUiCommand; docs/decisions/0005-agent-operated-relationship-workspace.md rejects arbitrary DOM automation.
findings.user_impact: The current build cannot silently message or schedule from Chat, but a future command added only in the client could drift from authorization, audit, and replay rules.
findings.recommendation: Define a versioned capability request containing actor, purpose, person, relationship context, command, affected object, expected version, consequence class, and idempotency key; validate it outside the model before applying any state change.
findings.verification: Fuzz ordinary questions and unsupported commands, tamper with person and context IDs, repeat idempotency keys, and request external writes; only scoped allowed commands may proceed, and every consequential request must stop at a separate approval.

findings.observation: The Agent contact form explicitly creates a new person from a recruiter-entered name, context, and first source. It does not silently merge, but it also does not show same-name or confirmed-handle candidates before creation.
findings.evidence: AgentCreatePersonCard submits scope_mode 'new_person' and displays 'It does not guess, merge, or contact anyone.' The live local submission created one person and relationship context from the first recruiter note.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can intentionally create a duplicate person and later face split evidence and reconciliation work, especially when the contact already exists under another context.
findings.recommendation: Before final creation, run deterministic account-scoped identity narrowing and show possible existing people with exact match reasons; keep create-new and leave-unresolved available without using name alone as an automatic merge.
findings.verification: Seed two same-name people and one exact confirmed handle; the form must never auto-merge, must show the exact-handle candidate, and must preserve a reversible recruiter decision with derivative recompilation.

findings.observation: The relationship data and sources persist with registered deletion paths, while the current Agent page-operation receipt is transient UI state and is not part of the append-only task history.
findings.evidence: A full reload restored the created person, context, and source from the backend but removed the recent local command receipt. Existing source-deletion tests cover governed derivatives, not the new transient page-operation receipt.
findings.user_impact: No evidence truth is lost, but an auditor or returning recruiter cannot distinguish whether Chat recently navigated, staged, canceled, or completed an internal operation.
findings.recommendation: Store compact operation events separately from evidence and confirmed relationship state, with purpose, object, status, cancellation, and retention semantics.
findings.verification: Complete, cancel, reload, and delete each internal command scenario; the timeline must retain the allowed audit event, retract governed derivatives when required, and never promote the receipt to a person fact.

strengths: Chat is scoped to one explicit person and relationship context.
Contact creation requires recruiter-owned source material and does not infer, merge, or contact anyone.
Page changes remain staged and visible on the affected object before confirmation.
Generated briefs retain snapshot and Context Manifest identifiers with governed reference counts.
No Agent command can currently send, schedule, update an external contact, or claim an unverified external result.
The UI distinguishes no_action from failure and does not infer person quality, personality, protected traits, or acceptance probability.
missing_evidence: Server-enforced Agent capability registry and durable operation receipts.
Possible-duplicate identity review inside the Agent create flow.
Cross-tenant and permission-change tests for Agent commands.
Mobile accessibility inspection of evidence and approval surfaces.
Field privacy and retention comprehension testing with recruiters.
open_questions: Which internal Agent operations should be stored as audit events, and which navigation-only operations should remain ephemeral?
What exact identity evidence is sufficient to suggest an existing person without creating pressure to merge?
